name: TOGAF EPIC v5 - width-walked, per-section-retrieved SAD
description: Contract for the v5 width layer executed by scripts/togaf_epic_v5.py. Stands on the v3 recursive pipeline (TOGAF skeleton floor, index planning, ICONIX robustness, citation gate, PDF SVG gate) and fixes the two structural causes of shallow output: (1) v3 gave every sub-section of a chapter the SAME chapter-level evidence bundle, so siblings paraphrased one fact-set - v5 shows the planner the real Neo4j schema and has it emit a read-only Cypher query per sub-section, so each section is written against its own retrieved slice; (2) v3 had seven fixed chapters and never enumerated the estate - v5 adds three chapters whose index is an inventory derived from disk and from the code graph itself (workflow contracts, modules resolved from CodeEntity paths, n-tier layers). Diagrams are rendered deterministically in code from each section's rows; the model selects a spec from a fixed vocabulary and never authors mermaid, because the PDF gate requires every mermaid block to render.
doctrine: The TOGAF skeleton is a FLOOR: the planner may extend a chapter, never drop a prescribed artifact.
Width chapters are INVENTORIED, not planned - their index is a function of the estate, so the document cannot silently drift from what exists.

Planner-authored Cypher is UNTRUSTED input: single statement, must start with MATCH, must RETURN, no mutating keyword, LIMIT forced and clamped. A rejected or failing query degrades the section to chapter evidence and is recorded honestly in the gate table.

The model NEVER authors mermaid. Diagrams are rendered in code from the section's own rows, because togaf_epic_pdf.mjs gates on svg_rendered >= mermaid_blocks and one malformed diagram would fail the whole build.
Every section cites [EV-*] labels that actually exist in its own evidence bundle; invalid citations fail the gate.
A section that retrieved nothing says so rather than inventing detail.

chapters.title: Layer Walk
chapters.index: inventoried from the ICONIX n-tier classification

gates.per_section: words >= word_floor AND >=1 citation AND a References block AND no invalid citation labels
gates.reported: a per-section table of words/citations/rows/diagram/query status is emitted into the document itself
